name: positional-index
title: positional-index: build, persist and open a compact binary index that records WHERE each term occurs
interface:
Module `lib/index-format.mjs`. Successor to the deprecated `inverted-index`: same three functions, same reader interface, with term positions added — everything the older statement demanded still holds.

```stub
export function buildIndex(docs: Array<{ id: string, title: string, body: string }>, meta: object): object;
export function writeIndex(dir: string, index: object): void;
export function openIndex(dir: string): object;
export const bodyPosition: (titleLen: number, j: number) => number;
```

- `buildIndex(docs, meta)` tokenizes each document with text-analyzer's `tokenize` and records
  every occurrence's POSITION, and returns an in-memory index that carries `meta` through unchanged.
- Position space, per document: title token j sits at position j, body token j at
  `bodyPosition(titleLen, j)` = titleLen + 1 + j. Position titleLen is never occupied, so the
  last title token and the first body token are never adjacent and no phrase can straddle the
  two fields. A term's title count is the number of its positions below titleLen, its body
  count the rest.
- `writeIndex(dir, index)` removes any previous index in `dir` (no stale file survives a
  rewrite), creates it, and serialises the index as a compact binary: a small JSON header
  holding counts, meta and section offsets, then variable-length-integer encoded document ids,
  document lengths, title lengths, the sorted term dictionary and the positional postings.
  The whole index must stay well under the size of the corpus it was built from.
- `openIndex(dir)` returns a reader over the files on disk, decoding lazily; it throws an Error
  mentioning the directory when the index is missing, and an Error mentioning the format when
  the magic/version bytes are wrong — an index written by an older format version is a version
  error, never silently misread. The reader exposes:
    reader.docCount   -> number of indexed documents
    reader.avgDocLen  -> mean weighted document length
    reader.meta       -> the object passed to buildIndex (docs, skipped, ...)
    reader.docId(i)   -> the id string of document i
    reader.docLen(i)  -> the weighted token length of document i
    reader.docTitleLen(i) -> the number of title tokens of document i
    reader.postings(term) -> Array<{ doc: number, body: number, title: number, positions: number[] }>,
                             ascending by doc, positions ascending and of length body + title,
                             empty for an unknown term.
nl_description: The storage half of the search engine, now positional: the on-disk shape of the index and the reader that queries go through. It owns the size dimension (index bytes relative to corpus bytes) and the cold-start half of the speed dimension — a query process must be able to open the index and pull one term's postings without parsing everything — and it is the only place that knows where a term sits inside a document, which is what makes exact-phrase search decidable. Also owns the "fully overwritten per run" rule: re-indexing a different corpus must leave nothing of the old one behind. Its gate runs the deprecated inverted-index gate too, so the frequency behaviour that predates positions cannot regress.
